answer.rationale: Rollback is ruled out because the release carries a mandatory security patch (compliance constraint). Add_capacity and route_read_replicas do not address primary-region write-path degradation during peak settlement load. Enable_circuit_breaker risks shedding customer writes — directly conflicts with the primary objective. Regional failover matches the degradation profile (primary-region confined, p99 climbing under heavy writes) and is supported by memory_b2 (March failover restored latency in minutes, traffic shifted cleanly, error rates recovered) and memory_b1 (rollback principle: 'fail fast, preserve the rest of the path' — failover is the write-preserving analog of that lesson). memory_b5 supports confidence that read-side scaling alone would not relieve this write-path issue. Verified memories are referenced only as priors; the action stands on its own merits. Uncertainty noted: failover on a write path during peak settlement is non-trivial and was not the exact scenario in b2 — recommend confirming primary-replica write consistency and running as a small, guarded test before declaring full cutover.
